__comment: Sprint 049 #049-30 (ADR-052 follow-up): panel tracks the latency of the impersonation_sessions UPDATE that runs on every authed request from a practitioner. If p50 climbs above 5ms sustained, we should consider the 5-second in-memory cache described in ADR-052. Import into Grafana via Dashboard -> Import -> paste this JSON.
__datasource: postgres-prod (adjust UID to match your datasource)
title: SHI impersonation UPDATE latency

panels.title: p50 / p95 UPDATE latency (ms)
panels.description: Latency of the resolve_impersonation UPDATE (auth middleware hot path). Enable auto_explain in Postgres OR use pg_stat_statements, whichever is available. Query below uses pg_stat_statements.

targets.rawSql: SELECT now() AS time, (total_exec_time / NULLIF(calls, 0)) AS avg_ms, (stddev_exec_time) AS stddev_ms, calls FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE query LIKE '%UPDATE impersonation_sessions%' ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Rolling window: p95 last 1h
panels.description: If this stays > 5ms for 15+ min, consider the ADR-052 cache.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (mean_exec_time + 2 * stddev_exec_time) AS p95_ms FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE query LIKE '%UPDATE impersonation_sessions%'
SELECT COUNT(*) AS active FROM impersonation_sessions WHERE ended_at IS NULL AND last_seen_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
SELECT COUNT(*) AS ended_24h FROM impersonation_sessions WHERE ended_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'

__runbook: 1. Import this JSON into Grafana: Dashboard -> Import -> paste -> pick your Postgres datasource -> Import.
2. If pg_stat_statements isn't enabled: ALTER SYSTEM SET shared_preload_libraries = 'pg_stat_statements'; restart Postgres; CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements;
3. If p95 > 5ms for 15+ consecutive minutes, escalate per ADR-052: consider the 5-second in-memory cache on the impersonation UPDATE path.
4. If active sessions > 50 simultaneously, validate the backend is coping -- cache becomes higher priority.
